# The future needs authentic, ethical, and transformative leadership.

**In a context marked by uncertainty and polarization, society is clamoring for ethical, collaborative, and purposeful leadership. This is the analysis of experts from EAFIT University, who believe that leaders are needed who listen and inspire hope, capable of building shared and sustainable futures.**

**In response to this need, EAFIT University launched In-Sight, its new center for studies and advocacy on impactful leadership, with the aim of connecting education, research, and action around the kind of leadership the world needs. The Center will foster conversations and publications that seek solutions to current challenges.**

- [Start](https://www.eafit.edu.co/)
- [News](https://www.eafit.edu.co/noticias)
- [EAFIT is in the News](https://www.eafit.edu.co/noticias/eafit-es-noticia)
- The Future Needs Authentic, Ethical, and Transformational Leadership

![Image: The future needs authentic, ethical, and transformative leadership](https://universidadeafit.widen.net/content/eac63253-beef-468b-8ac0-97334446cf99/web/Lideres-para-que.jpg?crop=yes&k=c&w=823&h=450&itok=JGaQ9xLt)

The In-Sight Center was presented as part of the forum "Leaders for what?", organized by EAFIT and the newspaper El Colombiano.

In a world marked by uncertainty, traditional leadership seems insufficient to address today's social, environmental, and political challenges. Faced with this reality, experts at EAFIT agree that new leadership models are needed that go beyond charisma or formal authority. These are leaders capable of listening, acting with purpose, and mobilizing others to build more just, sustainable, and collaborative societies.

This was the topic of discussion at the forum _"Leaders for What?"_ , organized by EAFIT University and the newspaper El Colombiano, where the new Center for Studies and Advocacy in Impactful Leadership, In-Sight, was launched. This center was created to study and research leadership, act as a trend observatory, and support organizations in promoting impactful leadership capable of driving sustainable transformations over time.

During the event, Claudia Restrepo Montoya, president of EAFIT University, emphasized that today's leaders must make sound decisions and act ethically in emotionally complex environments. “Leadership is a human condition. To speak of a leadership crisis is truly to speak of a human crisis, because what we're talking about is that either we have few people with the capacity to convene and influence others, or those who do manage to do so lack integrity.”

Alexander Garzón Lasso, director of In-Sight EAFIT, outlined five key areas for the leadership needed in the future: active listening and situational support; transformational inspiration; servant leadership; adaptability and intellectual stimulation; and authenticity and integrity. These components, he affirmed, must always be combined with critical thinking and empathy, as they “forge a leadership that drives individual and collective growth, turning challenges into opportunities and paving the way toward a shared future.”

The executive also emphasized the role universities must play as spaces for training leaders with real impact. This involves designing comprehensive educational experiences, connecting with the productive and social sectors, and fostering leadership that responds to major contemporary challenges. “The current context invites us to think about proactive leadership that positively transforms society. We are facing challenges related to environmental and social sustainability that call for reflection, and EAFIT has made progress in this area.”

In celebration of the University's 65th anniversary, this center is one of the landmarks whose central theme is: EAFIT is leadership.

#### Meaningful Leadership

Cristina Vélez Valencia, dean of the EAFIT School of Management, believes that today's leaders must be attentive to their surroundings, capable of identifying the new competencies, skills, and perspectives demanded by their contexts. "Business leaders must navigate the interests and needs of their stakeholders, which include their shareholders, of course, but also the community in which the company operates."

For her part, María Alejandra González-Perez, head of the Master's Program in Sustainability at EAFIT, offers a complementary perspective on the leadership demanded by the present. “We are going through uncertain times, and this requires leadership styles that allow us to see paths of hope, that guide organizations and teams toward a shared vision for the future, that help build bridges and connect, that are proactive—that is, that open up countless ways to reach a goal.”

Similarly, Professor María Alejandra adds that leadership should increasingly be understood as a collective practice rather than an individual exercise, and she insists on the need to highlight leadership guided by hope, integrity, and ethical awareness. Furthermore, she encourages us to recognize the value of managing uncertainty and chance through the philosophical concept of amor fati—"loving what is happening"—an attitude that does not imply resignation, but rather the ability to build upon circumstances, accept them, and extract the greatest possible learning from them.

Con la creación de In-Sight, EAFIT refuerza su compromiso con la formación de líderes que no solo respondan a las exigencias del presente, sino que también estén preparados para crear las condiciones de un futuro más humano y justo. El centro será una plataforma de análisis, diálogo y acción, al servicio de quienes ejercen o se preparan para practicar liderazgos con sentido.

En la [**página web de In-Sight**](https://www.eafit.edu.co/conexion-asuntos-publicos/centros-estudio-incidencia/in-sight) se puede consultar el informe _¿Está el liderazgo colombiano pensando en el futuro? Ranking y análisis del liderazgo posibilista en las empresas colombianas con mayor reputación_, un primer insumo para seguir entendiendo y transformando el liderazgo desde la evidencia y la reflexión crítica.
